punchline: A man who could not forget struggled to see patterns, in Foer's retelling of Luria's case.
thirty_sec: In 1928 a Russian journalist named S. told the psychologist Luria he had a remarkable memory, and Luria studied him for thirty years. He could keep formulas he did not understand, but his mind was cluttered and he struggled to generalize. Foer uses the case to argue that forgetting is part of how a mind works.
